subject.title: Cron fallback model works in normal session but LLM request fails when triggered via cron

question: Should work remain gated on a current-main live reproduction that identifies the firing watchdog, or should the v2026.6.10 transcript be treated as sufficient evidence to change timeout ownership now?
rationale: Current main has substantially different cron watchdog behavior, and the generic abort evidence cannot safely identify which timeout or cancellation scope needs repair.

options.title: Require current-main timeout trace
options.body: Reproduce with structured cron and embedded-run diagnostics, then repair only the watchdog or abort scope proven to fire.

options.title: Sponsor a defensive timeout refactor
options.body: Proceed from the older evidence by separating wall-clock, model-idle, and fallback cancellation scopes, accepting broader regression risk.

recommendation.title: Require current-main timeout trace
recommendation.body: Reproduce with structured cron and embedded-run diagnostics, then repair only the watchdog or abort scope proven to fire.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent fallback, timeout, and scheduled-run work makes this the strongest available owner for deciding the necessary proof threshold.
